title: Champions Week 2025: Glens Falls Black Bears - NewsBreak
text:
By Brian Rudman ,
1 hours ago
GLENS FALLS, NY ( NEWS10 ) — After winning the Section 2 Class B championship, the 2024 season would end in heartbreak for the Glens Falls Black Bears, falling just 6 points short in the state semifinals losing to the eventual champs, Port Jervis. Now the Black Bears are back to work as hungry as ever, looking to make a run to the state title game.
Runs to the state championship are not unfamiliar to some of the players on this roster. A handful of the athletes on the football team have been part of the back-to-back unbeaten, state title winning seasons for the Glens Falls Boys Basketball team.
“Obviously, we’ve had success with basketball,” said Senior Running Back and Cornerback, Jordan Baker. “So, we know what it means to play on a big stage like that. And I know all these guys on the football team want to get there ourselves to that state championship game.”
A huge part of the success last season was the Black Bears ability to find ways to win when it mattered most. Something that the coaching staff hopes gets carried into this season.
“I think Chase (McTague) will do that and I think Jordan Baker and Braydon Bennett and those guys will do that,” said Head Coach Pat Lilac. “Let’s get the rest of the cavalry going and have some confidence that when things get tough, we’re at our best.”
While the Black Bears did graduate a ton of talent, most notably Wide Receivers, Kellen Driscoll and Oscar Lilac, along with Quarterback, Brody Holcomb, they do return more than half their starters on each side of the ball. Among those returners is Baker, the teams star Running Back who will be a focal point of the offense once more.
“Jordan’s a really hard worker,” said Pat Lilac. “And he’s put on probably 10 pounds from last year and it was tough to bring his down last year.”
Glens Falls will have a new man under center this fall as Junior, Chase McTague, makes the switch from Slot Receiver to Quarterback. McTague has spent the past 2 seasons taking the backup reps at QB and working with Holcomb throughout that time has been crucial to McTague’s development at the position.
“You know, I learned a lot,” said McTague. “Us working in practice together every single day. He could throw the ball like anyone, like, better than anyone. So, being able to compete with him and battle every day and throw the ball with him every day, it was great.”
Making it to the Section 2 title game and winning it is always challenging regardless of the team. Having done it in the past, the Black Bears know what it’ll take to do it again this season.
“Rally on defense,” said Lilac. “We think we can come up with 11 to 15 kids on defense who are gonna swarm to the football. That’s what we’re trying to preach during the preseason. And also, just take care of the football, as always, just take care of the football.”
The road to the top of Class B in the Section will get even tougher this year. In addition to the already competitive group of teams Glens Falls had to overcome last year, the reigning champs of Class A, Averill Park, are dropping down a Class to B. The added challenge is something the Black Bears are looking forward to.
“Yeah, we’re excited for it,” said Baker. “It makes us thrilled. We wanna play these tough teams, we want to have these tough games when we’re in sectionals. That’s what we want.”
It will be straight into Class B play for the Black Bears who open the season on the road with a Week 1 matchup against Schalmont.
